mcqs.question: A constant force of 10 N is applied vertically upward on a block that slides 4 m horizontally on a frictionless surface. What is the work done by this force?

options.D: Undefined because the force is not horizontal

mcqs.explanation: Work is calculated as W = F·s·cosθ. Here the force is vertical (θ = 90°) while the displacement is horizontal, so cos90° = 0. Hence W = 10×4×0 = 0 J. The misconception that any force on a moving object does work is corrected by recognizing the directional component.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand work as a scalar quantity
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about work is correct?

options.A: Work has both magnitude and direction like a vector
options.B: Work is a scalar quantity; it has magnitude but no direction
options.C: Work can be negative only if the force is negative
options.D: Work is always positive because energy cannot be negative

mcqs.answer: Work is a scalar quantity; it has magnitude but no direction
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as the dot product of force and displacement, resulting in a scalar. It does not possess direction, though its sign (positive or negative) indicates whether energy is added to or removed from the system. Options A, C, and D misrepresent the nature of work.

mcqs.question: The most accurate definition of mechanical work done by a constant force is:

options.A: The vector product of force and displacement
options.B: The product of the magnitude of the force, the magnitude of the displacement, and the cosine of the angle between them
options.C: The change in kinetic energy of the object
options.D: The product of power and the time interval

mcqs.answer: The product of the magnitude of the force, the magnitude of the displacement, and the cosine of the angle between them
mcqs.explanation: Work W = F·s·cosθ captures both magnitude and the relative direction of force and displacement. Option A describes a cross product (torque), C describes the work‑energy theorem (a consequence, not the definition), and D defines work indirectly via power, which is not the primary definition.

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: A constant force of 20 N makes an angle of 30° with the direction of a 5 m displacement. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Using W = F s cosθ: W = 20 N × 5 m × cos30° = 100 × 0.866 = 86.6 J. Option B ignores the cosine factor, C uses only force or displacement, and D would be correct only if the force were perpendicular (θ = 90°).

mcqs.question: In which situation is the work done by the applied force positive?

options.A: Lifting a box upward against gravity
options.B: Pushing a crate backward while it moves forward
options.C: Holding a book stationary on a table
options.D: Applying a force perpendicular to the motion of a sliding block

mcqs.answer: Lifting a box upward against gravity
mcqs.explanation: Positive work occurs when the component of the force along the displacement is in the same direction as the displacement. Lifting the box upward means the applied force and displacement are parallel, giving positive work. Options B (force opposite displacement) gives negative work, C involves no displacement (zero work), and D gives zero work because the force is perpendicular.

mcqs.question: Which of the following examples illustrates negative work done by a force?

options.A: Friction acting on a sliding book that eventually stops
options.B: A person pulling a sled forward while it moves forward
options.C: A force applied perpendicular to the motion of a car
options.D: A force applied on an object that does not move

mcqs.answer: Friction acting on a sliding book that eventually stops
mcqs.explanation: Negative work occurs when the force component opposes the displacement. Friction opposes motion, so it does negative work, removing kinetic energy. Option B is positive work, C is zero work, and D is zero work because there is no displacement.

mcqs.question: Work done by a force on an object will be zero if:

options.A: The force is perpendicular to the displacement
options.B: The force is parallel and in the same direction as the displacement
options.C: The force is opposite to the displacement
options.D: The magnitude of the force equals the magnitude of the displacement

mcqs.answer: The force is perpendicular to the displacement
mcqs.explanation: When the angle between force and displacement is 90°, cosθ = 0, making W = F·s·cosθ = 0. Options B and C give positive or negative work respectively, while D is irrelevant because work depends on the component of force along displacement, not on equality of magnitudes.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand work as a scalar quantity
mcqs.question: Two separate forces each do 10 J of work on the same object during a process. What is the total work done on the object?

options.D: Cannot be added because work is a vector

mcqs.explanation: Work is a scalar, so the algebraic sum of individual works gives the total. 10 J + 10 J = 20 J. Option B would be true only if the works were equal and opposite (one positive, one negative). Options C and D incorrectly treat work as a vector quantity.
